## How we work

1. Assess: A fixed-scope review of your agents and controls, and a ranked list of what to fix.
2. Build: We design and build the controls, starting with one workflow on your data.
3. Hand over: Your team runs it, with the documentation and the evidence trail.

---

## AI governance assessment

Source: https://ailabconsulting.com/services/governance-assessment/

Start here if you run AI agents, or plan to, and need to know whether you could show an examiner what they did and who approved it. We review the agents in scope, test a sample of past decisions against your records, and tell you what to fix first.

What you get:

- An inventory of your AI agents and what each one can do
- Who approves each consequential action, and what gets recorded
- Gaps mapped to SR 11-7, SOX, DORA and the EU AI Act
- A ranked remediation plan and a one-page board summary

### How is the assessment priced?

It is fixed scope. We agree which agents and business areas are in scope before we start, and that sets the fee.

---

## Approval and audit architecture

Source: https://ailabconsulting.com/services/agent-authorization/

Agents can prepare payments, change records and contact customers. We design the controls that make those actions safe to allow. Each agent gets narrow permissions, consequential actions need a named approver, and every decision is recorded so an auditor's question becomes a query. Controls are enforced at the tool layer, including MCP servers and API gateways.

What you get:

- Access policies that limit what each agent can do (ABAC and ReBAC)
- Signed approvals tied to the exact action and its parameters, checked before it runs
- A decision record linking each action to its inputs, policies and approver
- Agents grounded in a governed knowledge graph, so they act on approved data

### Isn't OAuth enough to control an AI agent?

OAuth grants access for a session. An agent also needs approval for each consequential action, tied to its parameters and revocable until it runs. That can be built on top of OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange (RFC 8693).

---

## Compliant AI-assisted engineering

Source: https://ailabconsulting.com/services/ai-assisted-sdlc/

Banks and insurers want the speed of AI coding tools without gaps in change control. We set up the development lifecycle so the agent that writes a change never approves it, and so the evidence for each release is produced as you ship.

What you get:

- Rules for where AI may write code and where a person must approve
- Change requests stored as code and approved in normal review
- Release evidence produced by the pipeline
- Multi-model review of specs and code before sign-off
- Mapping to SOX, PCI DSS and DORA change controls

### Can regulated teams use AI coding agents and still pass an audit?

Yes, if the pipeline records who requested each change, who approved it and that tests ran. The agent that writes a change must never be the one that approves it.

---

## Fractional AI governance lead

Source: https://ailabconsulting.com/services/fractional-ai-leadership/

Mid-sized firms face the same AI expectations as large banks, with far smaller teams. A fractional lead sets your AI controls, reviews what gets built and reports to the board, and can step into hands-on work when needed.

What you get:

- AI policy, controls and operating model
- Architecture and vendor reviews
- Reporting to the board, risk committee and regulators
- A senior person to call when AI risk decisions come up

## Questions

### What does AI Lab Consulting do?

We help banks, credit unions, insurers and fintechs put AI agents into production with the approvals and records that examiners and auditors expect.

### What is an AI governance assessment?

A fixed-scope review of the AI agents you run: what each one can do and who approves its actions. You get the gaps, mapped to SR 11-7, SOX, DORA and the EU AI Act, and a ranked plan to close them.

### How do you stop an AI agent from taking actions nobody approved?

Consequential actions need a signed approval from a named person, tied to the exact parameters. The system that runs the action checks the approval first and refuses anything that does not match.

### Do you provide legal or compliance sign-off?

No. We design and build the controls and the evidence. Your compliance team, counsel and auditors make the legal calls.

### Do you work outside financial services?

Yes. We also build machine learning and computer vision systems, including for manufacturing and retail.

### Where are you based?

Laguna Beach, California. We work with clients remotely.
